summary:
Raconteur reports on Spendesk's European Spend Report 2026, which argues European SMEs are significantly overspending on software and AI tools. The report tracked 2,500 European businesses with 50 to 250 employees and found they collectively overspent by 69m euros, which extrapolates to roughly 7bn euros across the EU's 250,670 similarly sized firms. The main driver is vendor-level price variance: companies of similar size paying different prices for the same products, costing an estimated 40,000 euros extra per affected company per year. A further 3bn euros is wasted on duplicate tooling, including functionally duplicate AI tools.

Forrester Principal Analyst Faram Medhora cautions that the 7bn figure needs a narrower label, as it measures the annual gap in per-seat SaaS prices for 50 to 250 employee European companies, not total European software overspend. He notes some price variation is reasonable because pricing reflects negotiating strength, package, user count, contract term and timing. Problems arise when buyers cannot see what they own, what is actually used, or what peers pay, while vendors negotiate with a complete account view. His example: renewing 1,000 licences when only 650 employees use the product.

Recommended fixes center on centralisation: bringing contracts, invoices, usage and renewal dates into one view, starting major renewals early, benchmarking equivalent deals, removing unused licences before negotiating, and using SaaS and software asset management tools. Volume and usage-based pricing discounts are also suggested.

Top vendors by overspend among the sample: HubSpot (11.7m euros), Atlassian (11.3m), Salesforce (8.3m), Adobe (4.4m) and Notion (3.3m). Notion has the widest per-head variance. Germany and France show worse variance than the UK; France alone allegedly overspends 1.6bn euros annually. IDC's Stephen Elliot attributes duplication to fragmented teams and org structure.

Each European company overspending because of price variance pays extra annually
European businesses overspend on duplicate software, including functionally duplicate AI tools
The report tracked European businesses with headcounts between 50 and 250
The surveyed firms collectively overspent
Number of similarly sized companies in the EU used for extrapolation
claims.attribution: Eurostat Structural Business Statistics, cited by Spendesk

Overspend by the surveyed companies rose year over year
